name: John N. Simpson
role: Continental Land and Cattle Co. (Hashknife) cattleman of Dallas
bio: Col. John N. Simpson of Dallas, Texas, was a cattleman of the Continental Land and Cattle Co., whose Hashknife herds he drove north from Texas. In September 1884 he helped select the first train of black cattle shipped from Montana or Dakota, and in April 1885 he contracted to deliver cattle to the Marquis at Medora, overseeing the first delivery at the end of May. In 1885 he headed a Wyoming association committee seeking railroad passes for members, argued for a cattle trail through northwest Texas, and reported 6,500 Texas cattle past Dodge City. In 1886 the paper called him president of the Texas live-stock association, noted his large purchase on the Pecos, and reported a Hashknife drive under his charge stopped near Springer, New Mexico.
